 Bruce Arians Does Not Anticipate Future NFL HC Opportunity
 By Adam La Rose |
 at November 14, 2026 7:54 pm 
 Bruce Arians  said in a recent interview that he would welcome a return to the NFL sidelines . It remains to be seen if another head coaching opportunity arises for the Super Bowl winner.
 Arians was at the helm of the Cardinals from 2013-17. That was followed by a three-year run with the Buccaneers which ended with his 2021 retirement. If Arians is to return to an NFL role, it will only be as a head coach.
 “I’d rather coach it,”  he confirmed during an interview with Bob McManamon of The Arizona Republic .  “And I don’t want to be putting the team together and looking over someone else’s shoulder who’s coaching it. I’d rather put the team together, coach it and try to win another championship.” 
 Arians served as a Buccaneers senior football consultant after handing the coaching reins to Todd Bowles . His comments confirmed, though, that he has no interest in another opportunity along those lines or elsewhere in a front office. Arians has a career winning percentage of .624 as a head coach, and his health has improved after surviving cancer three times and undergoing heart surgery. On the other hand, age is an obvious factor which could leave Arians out of the league.
 “I don’t know, I doubt it,”  Arians replied when asked if he expects to receive a third opportunity to lead an NFL team.  “I mean nobody’s getting hired at 74, but I’m finally healthy for the first time in a while. If my health was this good, I would have never retired.” 
 The 2027 HC market is set to include the likes of  Mike Tomlin  and  Sean McDermott.  Those veteran coaches will no doubt generate significant attention during the upcoming hiring cycle, but Arians will be a name to watch given his desire to return to the fold via a second Tampa Bay gig or one sending him elsewhere. Even so, he apparently does not anticipate being hired to lead at staff at this point.
